There exist coefficients $\{a_j\}_{j=1}^{N_1}$ and a polynomial $P_{N_2}$ with

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that sigma_opt is the optimal choice among all sigma>0 and that the rate is 'theoretically optimal' for every beta. Every result, however, is an O(.) upper bound valid for some coefficients. Maximising an upper bound over sigma shows only that the bound is best at sigma_opt. Showing that no other sigma, or no other approximation, does better would require lower bounds on the error for each sigma, and none is proved. The rate is backed by a known lower bound (Stahl) only for beta=0; for beta>0 no optimality argument appears. The figures are numerical evidence, not proof.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the optimality claims as 'sigma_opt maximises the proved upper bound' (and rate-matching with Stahl for beta=0), or add matching lower bounds for the LP error for each sigma.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimality of sigma_opt, and the claim that the rate is optimal on S_beta and on corner domains for beta>0, are unsupported. Only upper bounds are established.
issues.title: Optimality of sigma_opt and of the rate is claimed but only upper bounds are proved
issues.why_classification: The upper-bound theorems survive, but an advertised conclusion (optimality among all sigma and of the rate for beta>0) must be withdrawn or receive a new lower-bound argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists a $\rho>1$ and polynomial $q^{(l)}_n$ of degree $n$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: In Walsh's Hermite formula the interpolation nodes are taken as Fekete points of the contour Gamma_rho itself. For such nodes, |l_{n+1}(z)|^{1/n} tends to the capacity of Gamma_rho both on Gamma_rho and inside it, including on S_beta. The ratio ||l_{n+1}||_{S_beta}/min_{Gamma_rho}|l_{n+1}| therefore gives no geometric factor rho^{-n}. Separately, for beta=0 the removed set (theta in [0,2]) is the whole unit disk centred at -d. That disk contains [0,1-d], so Omega_rho does not contain S_0=[0,1], contrary to the caption. For small beta the stated lower bound d on dist(Gamma_rho,S_beta) also fails. The decay estimate (Runge12)/(polynomial app), which gives N_2=O(sqrt(N_1)), is therefore not established as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: r_2 is analytic on C minus (-infinity,-C]. Interpolate at Fekete points of S_beta and apply Bernstein–Walsh with a level curve of S_beta's Green function lying in a neighbourhood that avoids (-infinity,-C] for every beta in [0,2). Then re-derive the T-polynomial bound on ||r_2|| on that neighbourhood.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed N_2=O(sqrt(N_1)) polynomial part, central to the conjectures, lacks a valid proof, in particular in the beta=0 (Stahl) case.
issues.title: Polynomial approximation of r_2 with N_2=O(sqrt(N_1)) is justified by an invalid Hermite/Fekete argument
issues.why_classification: A standard Bernstein–Walsh argument with corrected nodes and neighbourhood restores the geometric rate and N_2=O(sqrt(N_1)), so all claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 2 the residues at the s_k-poles contribute 1/(e^{(4pi^2 alpha/h)(T+alpha log(delta/C))}-1), which is about e^{-(2/(2-beta)) eta^2 T}. For sigma>sigma_opt with beta=0 this equals e^{-eta^2 T} with eta<1, which is much larger than e^{-T}. The asserted equality with O(T^l e^{-T}) therefore fails. In addition, the T^l prefactor is wrongly attached to the residue term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the residue term by O(e^{-(2/(2-beta)) eta^2 T}) without the T^l factor, as in (asy0k). This still gives the required O(e^{-eta^2 T}) for sigma>sigma_opt and O(T^l e^{-T}) for sigma<=sigma_opt.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the Case 2 proof of (errquad0) for sigma>sigma_opt rests on a false estimate.
issues.title: Case 2 Poisson-sum bound O(T^l e^{-T}) is false for sigma>sigma_opt
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the bound, using an estimate already in the paper, recovers (errquad0) unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem mainthmG sets sigma_opt to 2 sqrt(2-beta) pi/sqrt(alpha), which is sqrt(2) times the value in Theorem mainthm. Its proof only invokes the bounds of Theorems mainthm and mainthm2. For sigma between pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha) and 2 sqrt(2-beta) pi/sqrt(alpha), the statement asserts O(e^{-sigma alpha sqrt N}). The cited results give only the slower O(e^{-pi eta sqrt(2(2-beta)N alpha)}) there, and the eta in the second branch is computed with the wrong threshold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define sigma_opt in Theorem mainthmG as pi sqrt(2(2-beta))/sqrt(alpha), consistent with Theorem mainthm.
issues.overall_effect: The generalized rates (eq: rateG1)–(eq: rateG22) are unsupported in the misdefined sigma range.
issues.title: Theorem mainthmG uses a different sigma_opt threshold than the one proved
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of the definition makes the statement match the proof with no loss of content.
